channel.title: Interface Report
channel.description: Independent publication about AI products, agents, design, Human–AI interaction, engineering, startups and SaaS.

item.title: Figma just turned the design system into a production engine.
item.description: Figma’s new Weave node turns existing frames into controlled generative workflows, making the design system an active production layer for AI-assisted content.

item.title: Sponsored Agents turn the ad click into a conversation.
item.description: OpenAI is testing Sponsored Agents in ChatGPT, turning the post-click conversion surface into a labeled interactive conversation.

item.title: Salesforce is betting the enterprise UI becomes a live interface layer.
item.description: Salesforce AIforce brings governed data, workflows and permissions into AI interfaces, shifting enterprise software from fixed screens toward live interfaces.

item.title: AI incident disclosure is becoming part of the product trust layer.
item.description: OpenAI’s new misalignment-reporting framework points to a broader product pattern: trust depends on inspectable incidents, uncertainty and mitigation.

item.title: The AI tool picker is disappearing.
item.description: Anthropic is folding chat, Cowork and creation tools into one Claude interface, shifting AI UX from choosing a mode to expressing an outcome.

item.title: The dashboard-first era is ending. AI analytics is becoming a conversation.
item.description: OpenAI’s new Data agent points to a bigger product shift: analytics is moving from finding a dashboard to asking, inspecting evidence and acting.

item.title: GPT‑6 Astra is not your product. The capability boundary is.
item.description: A stronger model raises the ceiling, but product quality still depends on what the system is allowed to do, how it proves work and where it fails safely.

item.title: The Agents API changes the build-versus-orchestrate decision.
item.description: OpenAI is moving agent loops, context management and long-running execution behind an API.

item.title: Agent harness portability is becoming infrastructure, not a nice-to-have.
item.description: The abstraction is moving above the model.

item.title: Permission UX is becoming the real AI safety interface.
item.description: Scope, consent and temporary access become as important as answer quality.

item.title: The new AI trust loop is not answer → accept. It is answer → inspect → challenge.
item.description: Evidence provenance is becoming part of the interaction.

item.title: Full-duplex voice breaks the old turn-taking model. Your UI has to catch up.
item.description: Interruption, floor control and visible agent state become core voice-interface problems.

item.title: Stop making every AI feature a chat box.
item.description: Persistent state, comparison and consequential actions need more than conversation.

item.title: A production agent sandbox needs more than isolation.
item.description: Long-running agents also need scoped credentials, recoverable sessions and observable side effects.

item.title: Your average latency is lying to you. Tail latency is where AI products break.
item.description: Optimize the slow paths users actually feel.

item.title: AI pricing is becoming a product system, not a price page.
item.description: Usage, outcomes, credits and enterprise contracts require monetization infrastructure built for iteration.

item.title: Your next SaaS customer may be an agent. Is your product ready?
item.description: Products need a machine-usable path alongside the human UI.
